title: The body, feeling sick, and seeing a doctor
goal: Name parts of the body, describe symptoms to a doctor, and use the illness pattern where the subject isn't "I".
bekal: naming fifteen parts of the body
describing pain with درد ہے and لگ رہا ہے

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — ڈاکٹر کے پاس
dialogs.intro: Budi has been feeling unwell since last night. Ayesha takes him to the clinic near campus.

lines.speaker: ڈاکٹر:
lines.id: Come in, have a seat. What's the trouble?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: مجھے سر درد ہے اور بخار بھی ہے۔
lines.baca: mujhe sar dard hai aur buḵār bhī hai.
lines.id: I have a headache, and a fever too.
lines.literal: to-me head pain is and fever also is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: کل رات سے۔ مجھے نیند بھی نہیں آئی۔
lines.baca: kal rāt se. mujhe nīnd bhī nahīñ āī.
lines.id: Since last night. I couldn't sleep either.
lines.literal: yesterday night since. to-me sleep also not came(f).

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: جی، تھوڑا۔ اور کھانسی بھی ہے۔
lines.baca: jī, thoṛā. aur khāñsī bhī hai.
lines.id: Yes, a little. And I have a cough too.
lines.literal: yes, a-little. and cough also is.

lines.speaker: ڈاکٹر:
lines.text: منہ کھولیے۔ ہاں… گلا سرخ ہے۔ آپ نے کل کیا کھایا؟
lines.baca: muñh kholiye. hāñ… galā surḵ hai. āp ne kal kyā khāyā?
lines.id: Open your mouth. Yes… your throat is red. What did you eat yesterday?
lines.literal: mouth open-please. yes… throat red is. you (ne) yesterday what eaten?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: باہر سے کھانا کھایا تھا۔ بہت تیز تھا۔
lines.baca: bāhar se khānā khāyā thā. bahut tez thā.
lines.id: I'd eaten food from outside. It was very spicy.
lines.literal: outside from food eaten had. very spicy was.

lines.speaker: ڈاکٹر:
lines.text: کوئی خطرے کی بات نہیں۔ یہ دوا لیجیے، تین دن۔
lines.baca: koī ḵatre kī bāt nahīñ. ye davā lījiye, tīn din.
lines.id: It's nothing serious. Take this medicine for three days.
lines.literal: any danger of(f) matter not. this medicine take-please, three days.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: کھانے سے پہلے یا بعد میں؟
lines.baca: khāne se pahle yā bād meñ?
lines.literal: food from before or after in?

lines.speaker: ڈاکٹر:
lines.text: کھانے کے بعد۔ اور آرام کیجیے، پانی زیادہ پیجیے۔
lines.baca: khāne ke bād. aur ārām kījiye, pānī zyāda pījiye.
lines.id: After meals. And get some rest, drink plenty of water.
lines.literal: food of after. and rest do-please, water more drink-please.

notes: **Pain is expressed with the dative pattern, not with "I hurt".** مجھے سر درد ہے is literally "to me, head pain is". The subject of the sentence is **the pain**, not the person. A form that's also correct and a bit more detailed: میرے سر میں درد ہے ("there's pain in my head").

**Doctors use the word تکلیف to open an examination.** کیا تکلیف ہے؟ = "what's the trouble?", literally "what's the hardship?". The same word is used for putting someone out: تکلیف کے لیے معذرت ("sorry for the trouble"), آپ کو تکلیف ہوئی ("I've put you to trouble").

**Fever, cough, and a cold each have their own noun.** The words بخار (fever) · کھانسی (cough) · زکام (cold) · قے (vomiting) · دست (diarrhea). All are used with ہے, and the subject is مجھے — مجھے بخار ہے · مجھے کھانسی ہے · مجھے زکام ہے.

**The phrase کب سے means "since when", and the answer uses سے too.** کل سے (since yesterday), دو دن سے (for two days), صبح سے (since this morning). The postposition سے here means "since" — its fourth job, after "from", "with", and "than".

**The form کھایا تھا means "had eaten".** Adding تھا after a past verb marks that the event happened even **earlier** than the event being told — just like the English past perfect. You don't need to use it actively yet, but recognizing it will often help.

**The word تیز means both "fast" and "spicy".** کھانا تیز ہے = "the food is spicy". Related words to keep apart: گرم (hot in temperature), مصالحہ دار (heavily spiced), کڑوا (bitter), میٹھا (sweet), نمکین (salty), کھٹا (sour).

grammars.title: Describing your symptoms
body: There are two patterns, and both are correct. The first is shorter and more common; the second is more detailed and names the body part as a place.
after: The sentence you'll need most, and the one to memorize whole: **میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔** ("I'm not feeling well"). It covers every complaint at once and is always understood.

grammars.title: Parts of the body
body: Body parts always use the ordinary possessive — میرا سر · میری آنکھیں — never کے پاس. The rule from unit 17 applies fully.
after: ⚠️ Body parts that come in pairs are usually **plural**: میری آنکھیں دکھ رہی ہیں ("my eyes hurt"), میرے پاؤں تھک گئے ("my feet are tired"). Saying them in the singular sounds as if only one side has a problem — which is sometimes exactly what you mean.
The word دل does two jobs, just as "heart" does in English: the organ and the feelings. میرا دل نہیں چاہتا = "I don't feel like it", literally "my heart doesn't want".

sections.title: At the clinic and the pharmacy

blocks.title: Eight sentences for the clinic
items: Opening: میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔ ("I'm not feeling well") · مجھے دو دن سے بخار ہے۔ ("I've had a fever for two days")
Pointing to the problem: مجھے یہاں درد ہے۔ ("it hurts here") — while pointing, and it's the most useful sentence there is.
Asking about medicine: یہ دوا کیسے لینی ہے؟ ("how should I take this medicine?") · دن میں کتنی بار؟ ("how many times a day?") · کھانے سے پہلے یا بعد میں؟
Wishing well: **جلد صحت یاب ہوں۔** ("get well soon") — a sentence you'll **receive** from everyone, so it's good to know how to say it back. A shorter and very common one: اللہ شفا دے۔

You ask how to take the medicine: ____؟

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: مجھے سر درد ہے۔ — مجھے بخار ہے۔ — میرے پیٹ میں درد ہے۔ — مجھے کھانسی ہے۔ — میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔
کیا تکلیف ہے — مجھے کل سے بخار ہے۔ — یہ دوا کیسے لینی ہے — کھانے سے پہلے یا بعد میں — بہت شکریہ ڈاکٹر صاحب۔
مجھے سر درد ہے۔ — مجھے بھی بخار ہے۔ — میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔ — یہ دوا لیجیے۔ — اور آرام کیجیے۔
wave: Memorize one sentence: میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں ہے۔ It's enough to start a conversation with any doctor in Pakistan.
